title: Microsoft Teams: new content-sharing layouts for Teams events
summary: Hold: the briefing incorrectly says Microsoft Learn describes Manage what attendees see only as spotlighting people; Microsoft's release notes also describe controlling shared content. The roadmap facts, licensing and event-policy controls check out, but the stated Content only behaviour is not supported by the sources checked.

claims.quote: Organizers and presenters who have access to production tools will see updated layout options when sharing content in the "Manage what attendees see" experience for Teams events.

claims.where: controls[0]; summary; Why it matters; Governance controls
claims.claim: No admin UI setting or PowerShell parameter is documented for controlling the new content-sharing layouts.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams layouts Manage what attendees see admin PowerShell default; Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy layout attendees. Read set-up-events, plan-meetings, plan-events and Set-CsTeamsEventsPolicy; no layout selector policy found.

claims.claim: Microsoft Learn describes Manage what attendees see in events only as letting organisers decide who to spotlight.
claims.quote: An enhancement to the 'Manage what attendees see' feature now allows organizers and presenters to control when shared content is visible to attendees. This capability is available for meetings, webinars, and town halls.
claims.fix: Replace 'Microsoft Learn describes Manage what attendees see in events only as letting organisers decide who to spotlight' with 'The Teams events licensing overview describes Manage what attendees see as letting organisers decide who to spotlight'. Keep the following absence claim about the three layouts.

claims.claim: No Microsoft Learn page describes these three named layouts at the time of writing.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams Speaker focused Content focused Content only; Teams events content sharing layouts Content only; Teams events Speaker focused organizers. Read Learn results, events-licensing and plan-events; none describes this trio.

claims.claim: The sources do not ask administrators to act to enable these layouts.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams layouts Manage what attendees see admin PowerShell default; Teams events layout Speaker focused licensing default. Read roadmap, events-licensing, set-up-events and plan-events; no layout enablement action stated.

claims.claim: Teams admin center > Meetings > Events policies > policy > Events up to 1k attendees governs creation of events with up to 1,000 attendees.
claims.quote: In the left navigation of the Teams admin center, go to Meetings > Events policies. Select an existing policy or create a new one. ... turn the Events up to 1k attendees toggle On or Off.

claims.claim: Set-CsTeamsEventsPolicy -Identity <policy name> -AllowWebinars Disabled prevents the assigned organisers creating events with up to 1,000 attendees.
claims.quote: To prevent organizers with this policy from creating events with up to 1,000 attendees, run the following command: Set-CsTeamsEventsPolicy -Identity <policy name> -AllowWebinars Disabled

claims.claim: Teams admin center > Meetings > Events policies > policy > Events optimized for a large audience governs creation of events optimised for large audiences.
claims.quote: In the left navigation of the Teams admin center, go to Meetings > Events policies. Select an existing policy or create a new one. ... turn the Events optimized for a large audience toggle On or Off.

claims.claim: Set-CsTeamsEventsPolicy -Identity <policy name> -AllowTownhalls Disabled prevents the assigned organisers creating events optimised for large audiences.
claims.quote: To prevent organizers with this policy from creating events optimized for large audiences, run the following command: Set-CsTeamsEventsPolicy -Identity <policy name> -AllowTownhalls Disabled

claims.claim: Turning the event-creation setting Off after scheduling prevents the user running or starting the event.
claims.quote: If you change the value to Off after a user schedules an event, they can't run or start the event.

claims.claim: The two event-creation controls decide whether events can be created, not which sharing layout is offered.
claims.quote: Controls whether users with this policy can create events with up to 1,000 attendees, such as webinars. ... Controls whether users with this policy can create events optimized for large audiences, such as town halls.

claims.claim: Events policy controls apply to the users assigned the policy.
claims.quote: User-level policy for tenant admin to configure options for customizing Teams events experiences. Use this cmdlet to update an existing policy.

claims.claim: The Set-CsTeamsEventsPolicy reference describes the policy as still in preview.
claims.quote: This cmdlet allows you to configure options for customizing Teams events experiences. Note that this policy is currently still in preview.

claims.claim: Plan for Teams meetings lists Manage what attendees see as having no administrator control in meetings.
claims.quote: | Manage what attendees see | No control | Can decide who to spotlight during a meeting. |
